meta.keyPoints: Business Verticals: a) Urban Finance: [1][2] The company offers Two-Wheeler Finance, Home Loans & LAP, and Personal Loans. It offers two-wheeler financing solutions across urban India, serving over 90 lakh customers. It operates through 160+ branches and a wide network of 8,500+ sourcing points, with a presence in key states such as West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, and Gujarat. b) Rural Business Finance:[3] The company offers Rural Group Loans and Micro Finance (JLG) and Micro LAP against self-occupied residential property. It serves 1.6 Cr+ customers in rural India; it operates across 370+ districts in 17 states with 2,100+ meeting centre branches. c) Farmer Finance:[4] The company serves 13 lakh+ customers. It operates across 180+ branches in 16 states, engages 2,700+ dealers, and is well-penetrated across the top 5 OEMs through a non-captive distribution franchise. d) SME Finance:[1] The company offers loans to self-employed professionals, traders, and supply chain participants. e) Gold Finance:[5] [6] In Jun 2025, the company completed the acquisition of the gold loan business of Paul Merchants Finance through a slump sale. The gold finance business scaled up its network to 330 branches by Q4 FY26, with about 200 new branches added since the acquisition in Jun 2025.

assumptions._note: L&T Finance (consolidated) lender model, as of 30-Sep-2026 on a Q1FY27 basis. AUM = the company's consolidated 'book' (retail + wholesale loans, ₹1,21,728 cr at Mar-26); it excludes the net security receipts (SRs, ₹4,808 cr) from wholesale loans sold to ARCs, which sit in investments. Sources: Q1FY27 presentation and call (13-Jul-2026); Q4FY26 presentation and call (27-Apr-2026); Annual Reports FY22, FY24, FY25 and FY26 for revenue splits and credit losses; Screener.in for statements (FY24 revenue and expenses put on the audited basis by tools/authoring/LTF.patch.js).

history._why: aum = consolidated book at March (company presentations: FY19-FY20 Q4FY20 deck p61, FY21 Q4FY21 deck p51, FY22 Q4FY22 deck p51, FY23-FY26 Q4FY26 deck p66/p68). provisions = all credit and investment losses in the audited consolidated P&L: impairment on financial instruments + net loss on derecognition (write-offs) + net loss on fair value changes (mostly mark-downs of security receipts and wholesale assets), the same definition Motilal Oswal uses; FY23 also includes the ₹2,687 cr exceptional fair-valuation loss on the wholesale book (reclassified for accelerated sell-down), which Screener puts in Expenses. feeIncome = revenue from operations less interest income (fees and commission incl. insurance distribution, dividends, fair-value gains). Up to FY24 most insurance distribution income sat in 'other income', which Screener shows below the line, so FY21-FY24 fee ratios are understated.

base._why: Paid-up equity capital ₹2,504.39 cr at ₹10 face value on 31-Mar-2026 (Annual Report FY26 balance sheet) = 250.44 cr shares; Screener's FY26 profit ÷ EPS gives 250.5 cr. ESOP allotments add ~0.1 cr a year (250.57 cr implied by Q1FY27 book value per share); not modelled.

assumptions._aumGrowthWhy: FY27 guidance 'AUM growth of over 20%' (27-Apr-2026); Lakshya 2031 '20%+ CAGR'. Q1FY27 book +27% YoY and +6.5% QoQ even after management turned away ₹1,000-1,200 cr of disbursements. FY26 delivered 24.5% against '20%+' guidance. We take 24% for FY27E (the quarterly run-rate of ~5% for the rest of the year), fading to 21% and 20% as the personal-loan base effect wears off. Brokers: Emkay 23%/21%, Motilal Oswal ~26%/23%.

aumBuild._why: Illustrative business build (GAM), checked in LTF.ctx.js to sum to the model AUM within 1%. Growth % per year; gold loans and the wholesale run-off in ₹ cr. Guidance: 400-500 new gold branches, 150-200 micro-loan and 150-200 micro-LAP branches in FY27; wholesale book to run off (no new lending since FY24).

assumptions._yieldOnAumWhy: Interest income ÷ average book (our basis; includes treasury income on ~₹14-18k cr of cash and investments): 15.0% FY25, 15.1% FY26 (company basis 15.20% / 14.71% on its own interest-income definition). Q1FY27 revenue ÷ average book (annualised) was 16.6% incl. fees, vs 16.3% in FY26. The mix shifts to personal loans (~16% yield), micro-LAP and gold, and away from home loans and the ₹2,220 cr wholesale book (11-12%); mortgages are the only floating-rate book. We hold the yield broadly flat (+5-10bp), in line with management's 'NIM + fees 10-10.5%' corridor.
assumptions._feeIncomePctWhy: Fees & other operating income ÷ average book: 1.29% FY25, 1.18% FY26. Distribution income (insurance) was ₹1,047 cr in FY26 (life ₹880 cr, general ₹151 cr): 0.95% of average book and ~26% of PBT. IRDAI's consultation paper (23-Sep-2026) proposes a 2% cap on credit-life commission (28% now), nil on loan-packaged motor TP, 5% on health, and a ban on compulsory bundling (IIFL summary); IIFL estimates a 12% PBT hit for LTF even after 50% mitigation, the highest among NBFCs. We assume a third of distribution income is lost from FY28E net of mitigation (−0.30pp of book); the bear case loses most of it.
assumptions._costOfFundsWhy: Interest expense ÷ average Screener borrowings: 7.1% FY25, 6.65% FY26 (the company's weighted average cost of borrowing was 7.35% in FY26; our measure, on the average of year-end borrowings, runs ~0.7pp lower, so we model the change rather than the level). Q1FY27 WACB 7.20%; CFO guides FY27 WACB to 7.35-7.40% assuming one or two rate rises (13-Jul-2026); a majority of economists polled expected a 25bp repo hike at the October policy (Moneycontrol, 28-Sep-2026). FY28E carries a full year of higher rates; LTF is AAA-rated with PSL access, so it reprices less than AA peers.
assumptions._opexPctWhy: Operating expenses incl. depreciation ÷ average book: 4.2% FY25, 4.02% FY26 (company 4.31% / 4.11%); Q1FY27 3.94% annualised (company 4.03%). FY27 adds 400-500 gold branches, 150-200 micro-loan and 150-200 micro-LAP branches and AI build-out; Lakshya 2031 guides opex to book of 3.75-4.0% and opex + credit cost of 5.75-6.0%. Operating leverage only from FY28E.
assumptions._creditCostWhy: Credit and investment losses ÷ average book: 2.53% FY25, 2.50% FY26 (company 2.50% / 2.54% after macro-prudential releases of ₹400 cr / ₹450 cr; 2.93% / 2.95% before). Q1FY27 2.54% with no release. Guidance: 2.0-2.2% by Q4FY27; 'for modelling, plug 2-2.2%' for FY28; below 2% over Lakshya 2031. Slippages fell from ₹944 cr (Q1FY26) to ₹402 cr (Q4FY26). We are 10-15bp above the guided path: FY27E 2.40% (a 2.54% → ~2.2% glide), FY28E 2.25% and FY29E 2.15%, because personal loans (14% of the book, unseasoned at this size) and resumed microfinance growth push the other way and the FY26 ROA guidance (2.4-2.5%) was only just met.
assumptions._taxRateWhy: FY26 effective 25.4% (current ₹1,070.65 cr, deferred −₹55.35 cr on PBT ₹3,998 cr); statutory 25.17%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend ₹2.75 a share for FY25 and FY26 (FY26: 23% of EPS ₹11.92), paid in Q1 of the next year (~₹700 cr). We keep a 23% payout.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Screener 'other income' was ₹16 cr in FY25 and −₹26 cr in FY26 (₹3 cr other income less the ₹28.5 cr one-time labour-code charge). Q1FY27 ₹30 cr (not explained; the CFO said nothing material). We keep the Q1 figure for FY27E and nothing after. SR recoveries are excluded: management will use them to build macro-prudential provisions, not book them as profit.

bs._why: Cash, bank balances and investments were ₹18,523 cr at Mar-26 (15.2% of book), incl. ₹4,808 cr of net security receipts (down from ₹6,770 cr in FY24 and ₹5,862 cr in FY25). We let SRs keep resolving (~₹1,000 cr a year, the FY26 pace; 'three to four years', CFO) and hold the rest of the liquidity at ~11% of book, so the ratio falls ~1pp a year; the money is redeployed into loans.

assumptions._capitalRaiseWhy: No raise needed: Tier 1 17.14% and CRAR 17.89% in Jun-2026 (minimum 15%); debt/equity 4.09x. The last equity raise was the ₹3,000 cr rights issue of FY21.

valuation._why: Ke = 6.5% + 1.15 × 6% = 13.4%. Beta 1.15 (as for Cholamandalam): AAA-rated with L&T as parent, but ~45% of the book is unsecured (microfinance, personal loans, much of SME) and microfinance has had three losses cycles in a decade. sustainableRoe 15%: above anything LTF has earned since FY19 (18% at the wholesale peak; 11-12% in FY25-26) and below the 16-18% Lakshya 2031 target. g = 10% long-run book growth. Residual income fades ROE to 15% over 8 years, payout rising to 30%, 6% terminal growth.

methods.name: P/B
methods.why: The street's method (Motilal Oswal, Emkay, ICICI Securities and ICICI Direct: 2.7x FY28E book). 1.6x = LTF's own median forward P/B since Apr-2024, the first full year as a single 94%+ retail lender (1.7x; the house window from Apr-2021 gives 1.3x but is dominated by the wholesale-and-AMC holding company of FY22-FY24), × listed lenders' P/B move vs five-year medians (−6.6%, eight peers excluding LTF) × growth regime 1.00 (the retail-era window already priced the recovery in ROE). Bull 2.2x = 75th percentile since Apr-2024 (≈ the market's level in 2025-26 before IRDAI); bear 1.2x = lowest since Apr-2024.

methods.name: Justified P/B
methods.why: (ROE − g) ÷ (Ke − g) = (15 − 10) ÷ (13.4 − 10) on book at the 12-month target date.

methods.name: Residual income
methods.why: Book plus the present value of profit above the 13.4% cost of equity, ROE fading to 15%, rolled forward 6 months.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Cross-check only (UBS uses 18x FY28E EPS). 12x = median forward P/E since Apr-2024 (15.1x; since Apr-2021 13.0x reported, 12.6x after removing FY23, when EPS was a loss before the mutual-fund sale gain) × listed-lender P/E move vs five-year medians (−19.7%) × growth 1.00. Bull 17x = 75th percentile since Apr-2024; bear 11x = lowest since Apr-2024.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Lakshya 2031 on schedule: AUM +26/23/22%, IRDAI softens its caps so only a sixth of distribution income is lost, credit cost meets guidance (2.2% FY27E, ~2.0% FY28E, below 2% in FY29E) as Cyclops reaches microfinance and mortgages; ROE ~16% by FY29E and 17% long run.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: A weak (El Niño) monsoon and another microfinance cycle: AUM +19/16/15%, credit cost back to ~3% (FY25's level before provision releases), most insurance distribution income lost to IRDAI caps (−0.6pp of book vs FY26), funding 25bp dearer; ROE stuck near 10-11%, 12% long run.

cover.headline: A rebuilt retail lender already priced for its 2031 targets, and the NBFC most exposed to IRDAI's commission caps
cover.lead: L&T Finance (LTF), two-thirds owned by Larsen & Toubro, has turned itself from a wholesale-heavy lender into a 98% retail one in four years: rural group loans, farm equipment, two-wheelers, personal loans, home loans and LAP, SME and, since Jun-2025, gold loans. Q1FY27 was its best quarter yet (book +27%, profit +29% to ₹902 cr, credit cost 2.54%, ROE 12.71%), but ROE is still below a ~13% cost of equity, and ~26% of FY26 pre-tax profit came from selling insurance, which IRDAI proposed on 23-Sep to cap. The street values LTF on **P/B (2.7x FY28E book)**. We forecast EPS of ₹15.5 / ₹18.0 / ₹22.6 for FY27-29E and ROE of 13-15%, including a haircut for the IRDAI proposal. Applying **1.6x to Sep-28E book of ₹146** (LTF's own 1.7x median since it became a retail lender in 2024, adjusted for the sector's −6.6% move) gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL**. Every cross-check is below the price (P/E ₹244, justified P/B ₹192, residual income ₹186); at ₹265 the market already assumes a ~{{dcf.impliedRoe|pct0}} ROE for ever. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The repair is done; the returns are not
arguments.p: Retail is 98% of the book (51% in FY22), the wholesale loans are down to ₹2,098 cr, and NIM plus fees is a steady 10.3-10.5% of the book. But ROE was 11.25% in FY26 and 12.71% in Q1FY27, and LTF missed its own Lakshya 2026 ROA goal (2.8-3.0%; 2.40% delivered). The new goal, ROE of 16-18% by FY31, needs credit costs below 2%, against 2.45-3.44% in every year from FY22 to FY26. We model ROE of {{F.roe.0|pct}} / {{F.roe.1|pct}} / {{F.roe.2|pct}}.

arguments.h: Growth is fast and broad, but leans on the riskiest products
arguments.p: Book growth of 27% in Q1 came from personal loans (+80%), gold (+182%), micro-LAP (+169%), LAP (+38%) and SME (+28%); microfinance resumed growing (+18%). Unsecured loans (microfinance, personal and SME) are ~44% of the book. Project Cyclops, LTF's in-house underwriting engine, has a two-year record only in two-wheelers. We take 24% AUM growth for FY27E (guidance "over 20%") and keep credit cost above the guided path.

arguments.h: IRDAI: the most exposed listed NBFC
arguments.p: Insurance distribution income was ₹1,047 cr in FY26, 26% of pre-tax profit, most of it credit-life cover sold with microfinance and other loans. IRDAI's paper proposes a 2% cap on credit-life commission (28% today) and a ban on compulsory bundling; IIFL puts LTF's hit at 12% of PBT even after mitigation. We cut fee income by 0.30% of the book from FY28E (~₹1.5 of EPS); the bear case loses most of it. The stock fell from ₹313 to ₹265 in the last two weeks of September.

arguments.h: Valuation: you pay today for the 2031 plan
arguments.p: At ₹265 LTF trades at 1.9x our FY28E book and 14.7x FY28E EPS, above its 1.7x median forward P/B since Apr-2024 (and 1.3x since 2021), for an ROE that only reaches the cost of equity in FY28E on our numbers. Our 1.6x Sep-28E book gives {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}). The street's 2.7x FY28E book assumes ROE heads to 16-18% and that IRDAI does not bite.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): is credit cost on the path to 2.0-2.2% by Q4FY27, and does personal-loan quality hold after +80% growth?
IRDAI's insurance-distribution reforms: consultation paper of 23-Sep-2026, comments due 25-Oct-2026; a 2% credit-life cap would remove most of LTF's ₹1,047 cr of distribution income.
RBI's October 2026 policy: most economists polled expected a 25bp repo hike; the CFO budgets FY27 WACB at 7.35-7.40% (Q1 7.20%).
Monsoon and El Niño: rural books (microfinance, tractors, 39% of the book) are the first place a weak kharif would show; LTF says reservoirs are adequate.
The Q4FY27 test: management has committed to an ROA of at least 2.8% in Q4FY27 (2.48% in Q1).
Security-receipt resolutions (₹4,808 cr net): recoveries go to provisions, not profit, but would free capital and remove a ~20bp ROA drag.

sections.title: A rural-and-urban retail lender with 2.9 crore customers, built on the L&T name

blocks.p: L&T Finance is the lending arm of Larsen & Toubro, India's largest engineering and construction group, which owns 66%. It is an upper-layer NBFC (the RBI's tier for the largest non-bank lenders), takes no public deposits and is rated AAA by all four domestic agencies, a rating the agencies tie to L&T's support. It makes money the way every lender does: on our measures it borrowed at ~6.7% in FY26 (the company's own weighted cost of borrowing was 7.35%), lent at ~15%, earned another ~1.2% of the book in fees (mostly commission for selling insurance), and kept what was left after operating costs (~4.0%) and credit losses (~2.5%). In FY26 interest income was ₹16,616 cr of its ₹17,914 cr revenue, and net profit ₹2,983 cr.

It serves two very different customers. **Rural** (39% of the book): women borrowing ₹40,000-1,00,000 in joint-liability groups through 2,184 meeting-centre branches in ~2 lakh villages, farmers buying tractors, and micro-LAP. **Urban** (61%, incl. SME and gold): two-wheeler buyers, salaried personal-loan customers sourced through big-tech apps, home loans and LAP, small businesses and, since Jun-2025, gold-loan customers. Unsecured lending (group loans, personal and SME loans) is ~44% of the book, more than at any large NBFC except Bajaj Finance and SBI Cards.

blocks.callout: **Why this matters:** LTF is really two lenders under one brand. The rural franchise (group loans, tractors) is large, old and profitable in good years, but it has had a loss cycle every three to four years (demonetisation 2016, Covid 2020-21, over-indebtedness 2024-25). The urban franchise is newer and is where growth now comes from: personal loans, gold and LAP grew 38-182% in the year to Jun-2026. Neither has a cheap-money advantage; the L&T name buys a AAA rating, not deposits.

sections.title: From a wholesale-heavy holding company to a retail lender, at the cost of a lost decade

blocks.p: L&T Finance Holdings listed in 2011 as the holding company for L&T's lending, mutual-fund and wealth businesses. Until FY21 more than half of its book was infrastructure and real-estate lending. When that book soured after 2018, the company ran a four-year clean-up: it raised ~₹3,000 cr in a rights issue (FY21), sold the wealth business (L&T Capital Markets, Apr-2020) and the mutual-fund business (Nov-2022), sold most wholesale loans to asset-reconstruction companies for security receipts (FY23), merged its lending subsidiaries into the listed company (Dec-2023) and renamed itself L&T Finance (2024). The pattern for shareholders: book value per share grew only ~9% a year from FY19 to FY26, and the share price did not pass its Sep-2017 high (₹193) until Jun-2025.

sections.title: Microfinance is out of its crisis and consumer credit is booming, but rates and regulators have turned

blocks.p: LTF's biggest single book is rural group lending, so the microfinance cycle matters most. The industry went through an over-indebtedness crisis in 2024-25: borrowers with loans from four or more lenders defaulted in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Bihar, lenders' collections fell and credit costs spiked. The industry book has since shrunk from a peak of ~₹4.4 lakh cr to ~₹3.3 lakh cr, the share of customers with more than three loans is below 5%, and the industry body MFIN's guardrails (no more than three lenders, ₹2 lakh total group-loan debt) now apply (CEO, 13-Jul-2026). LTF came through better than most: in Q1FY27 96.5% of its group-loan book was current against 77.9% for the industry (CRIF High Mark), and its 0-DPD collection efficiency was back at 99.8%.

Urban consumer credit is the opposite story: strong. LTF's CEO reports record two-wheeler sales at dealers in May-June 2026, personal-loan demand through big-tech platforms is rising, and UBS (23-Sep-2026) expects ~30% personal-loan growth for NBFCs. Gold loans boomed with the gold price, though the RBI's new gold-loan rules (tiered loan-to-value and need assessment, from April 2026) cut originations across the industry for a month. The risks sit elsewhere: the monsoon was 14% below normal by 10-Jul (El Niño), and money got dearer in September: the Nifty fell ~5% for the month on foreign selling, Brent was ~$106 and most economists polled expected a 25bp repo hike in October. Then IRDAI's 23-Sep proposal hit every lender that sells insurance with its loans.

Among the listed lenders we track, LTF had the lowest FY26 ROE except Poonawalla (11.1% on Screener's figures) and a mid-table ROA (2.27%), yet trades at 2.3x trailing book, close to HDB Financial (2.5x) and well above M&M Financial (1.7x), which earns a similar ROE. Its market value was ₹0.66 lakh cr on 30-Sep-2026.

sections.title: Gold and SME are the new growth bets; the wholesale legacy is down to ~5% of the book

blocks.h: Gold loans: bought in, then built out fast

blocks.p: LTF entered gold loans on 9-Jun-2025 by buying Paul Merchants Finance's gold business as a slump sale: a ₹1,335 cr book, 130 branches and 696 staff for ₹712 cr in cash (net assets ₹530 cr, goodwill ₹182 cr). It has since added ~200 branches (343 in Jun-2026), built its own loan-origination system ("Project Canyon") in four months, and grown the book to ₹3,829 cr (+182%). It plans ~500 more branches in FY27, about 1.4 a day. Q1FY27 disbursements fell 31% from Q4 as the RBI's new gold-loan rules took effect in April; management expects normal growth from Q2.

blocks.p: What we do not know matters: LTF does not disclose gold yields, losses or branch-level profitability, and the business competes with Muthoot, Manappuram and banks that have run gold branches for decades. New branches take time to fill; until they do, gold adds cost (part of FY27's opex) before it adds profit. We assume ₹7,500 cr of gold book by Mar-27 and ₹20,500 cr by Mar-29 (~9% of the book), a GAM estimate.

SME finance (₹8,884 cr, +28%) lends to self-employed professionals, traders and supply-chain participants, mostly unsecured. Disbursements fell 15% QoQ in Q1FY27 (₹1,567 cr) because management cut lending to sectors exposed to the West Asia conflict. Cyclops sorts SME borrowers into "premium", "core" and "value" segments; LTF now buys CGTMSE guarantees on the value segment and launched an AI fraud-screening tool ("Argus") in the quarter.

blocks.h: The wholesale legacy: how much of the old LTF is left

blocks.p: At its peak the wholesale book (infrastructure, real-estate and "defocused" loans) was ₹63,052 cr (FY19, 64% of the book). It is now ₹2,098 cr (infrastructure ₹1,257 cr, real estate ₹841 cr), all standard except one real-estate account (Supertech, ~61% provided). Much of the rest was sold to asset-reconstruction companies in FY23 for security receipts (SRs): net SRs were ₹6,770 cr in FY24, ₹5,862 cr in FY25 and ₹4,808 cr in FY26, held at a 68% provision cover. Together, ~₹6,906 cr (~5.3% of the book) of legacy money earns little or nothing; the CFO expects most of it to resolve over "three to four years", and the CEO puts the ROA drag at ~20bp.

Management has promised to use SR recoveries to build provisions rather than book them as profit, so we model no gains, only the run-off (liquidity falls ~1pp of the book a year as SRs resolve, cutting borrowings). The upside, if resolutions come faster, is to capital and to the ~20bp ROA drag, not to reported earnings.

blocks.p: LTF guides on "NIM + fees" on its own basis: 10.67% in FY24, 10.59% in FY25, 10.33% in FY26 and 10.47% in Q1FY27, inside a 10-10.5% corridor it has held for three years. blocks.p: **Fee income is the line to watch.** Fees and commission were ₹1,233 cr in FY26, of which distribution income (selling insurance) was ₹1,047 cr: life insurance ₹880 cr (mostly credit-life cover sold with group, personal and two-wheeler loans), general insurance ₹151 cr and other products ₹17 cr. blocks.p: LTF's credit cost on its own basis was 3.44% in FY22, 2.77% in FY23, 2.45% in FY24, 2.50% in FY25 and 2.54% in FY26. blocks.p: **The March 2026 provision reshuffle.** In the annual model refresh LTF moved ₹301 cr of management overlays out of Stage 3 (and ₹11 cr out of Stage 2) into Stage 1, and folded the last ₹125 cr of macro-prudential provisions into the model. sections.title: Funding: AAA thanks to L&T, well matched, but wholesale money with no deposits

blocks.p: LTF borrowed ₹1,15,423 cr in Jun-2026 (₹93,768 cr a year earlier) from banks (priority-sector and other term loans), private and retail debentures, commercial paper and foreign borrowings (ECB). It takes no public deposits. All four domestic agencies rate it AAA, which the company attributes to its business mix and to "strategic importance and strong support from L&T"; S&P (BBB) and Fitch (BBB-) rate it at India's sovereign level, which opens the door to foreign borrowing the CFO says he is not using yet. Its weighted average cost of borrowing was 7.35% in FY26 and 7.20% in Q1FY27, and it expects 7.35-7.40% for FY27 assuming one or two rate rises. Priority-sector bank loans (available because most rural loans qualify) keep it cheaper than AA-rated peers.

sections.title: Capital: plenty today (Tier 1 17%), being used up by 25% growth

blocks.p: Capital adequacy was 17.89% in Jun-2026 (Tier 1 17.14%) against RBI minimums of 15% and 10%. It was 22.8% in FY24 and 22.3% in FY25: the four years of shrinkage left LTF over-capitalised, which is one reason its ROE was so low. Growth is now using that capital up: debt/equity rose from 3.61x (Mar-25) to 4.09x (Jun-26) and Tier 1 fell ~3.6pp in five quarters. With a 23% payout, equity grows ~10% a year from profit against 20-24% book growth, so our model takes AUM from {{fin.leverage.11|n2}}x equity in FY26 to {{fin.leverage.14|n2}}x in FY29E. The last equity raise was the ~₹3,000 cr rights issue of FY21; we assume none in our forecast.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** capital is not a constraint before FY29 at our growth rates, and leverage of ~5.5x by FY29E is still below Cholamandalam (~7x) or Shriram. But part of the ROE improvement LTF promises (16-18% by FY31) is simply leverage: more debt on the same equity. That raises returns in good years and losses in bad ones. If growth ran at 25%+ for long, LTF would need equity around FY30, or a lower payout.

sections.title: A lost decade for shareholders, then four years of repair: profit has nearly tripled since FY22, ROE is still only 11%

blocks.p: L&T Finance's ten-year record has two halves. Up to FY19 it was a fast-growing wholesale-plus-retail lender: profit rose from ₹855 cr (FY15) to ₹2,232 cr (FY19) and ROE reached 18%. Then the infrastructure and real-estate book went bad after the IL&FS default (2018), Covid hit, and profit fell to ₹949 cr in FY21 (ROE 5.8%). FY22-FY23 were clean-up years: the wholesale book was sold down, a ₹2,687 cr fair-value loss was booked in FY23 (offset by the ₹2,575 cr gain on selling the mutual-fund business), and continuing operations lost money that year. Since FY24 the business has been a retail lender, and profit has grown 13-51% a year to ₹2,983 cr in FY26. But because book value kept growing, ROE has only climbed from 10.3% to 11.1%.

blocks.p: A lender's moat shows up as a lasting gap between what it earns and its cost of equity. sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audits, but provision releases, related-party fees and two sets of definitions need watching

blocks.p: We rate accounting **AMBER**. Joint auditors Brahmayya & Co and T R Chadha & Co LLP gave an unmodified opinion on FY26. Disclosure is good on stages, collections and the wholesale run-off, weaker on segment profitability. Five things deserve attention:

bullets: **Provision releases flattered FY25 and FY26.** LTF released ₹400 cr (FY25) and ₹450 cr (FY26) of macro-prudential provisions against microfinance losses, ~11% of each year's PBT. The buffer is now gone; reported credit cost from FY27 is "clean" but unprotected.

**Insurance income and the parent.** Distribution income of ₹1,047 cr (~26% of PBT) is real cash, but it is exactly what IRDAI proposes to cap. LTF also paid L&T a brand licence fee of ₹156 cr in FY26 (₹136.53 cr in FY25), ~3.9% of PBT: disclosed, but a recurring transfer to the controlling shareholder.

**Two definitions of the same P&L.** The presentation shows interest income of ₹15,948 cr and fee & other income of ₹1,973 cr for FY26; the accounts show ₹16,616 cr and ₹1,298 cr. The company moves ~₹670 cr of treasury and other income into "fees". NIM + fees is the same either way, but core NIM and fee ratios are not comparable with peers.

**Security receipts.** ₹4,808 cr of SRs are carried at fair value with a 68% provision cover; recoveries are being parked in buffers rather than booked as profit. That is conservative, but SR values are management estimates of real-estate and infrastructure recoveries.

**One-offs in history.** FY23 profit (₹1,623 cr attributable) included a ₹2,575 cr gain on the mutual-fund sale and a ₹2,687 cr fair-value loss on wholesale loans; FY26 includes a ₹28.5 cr labour-code charge. We adjust the P/E history for FY23 (valuation chapter).

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** a lender that has finished an impressive clean-up: 98% retail, a AAA rating from its L&T parentage, growth of 25-27% across every business, credit cost falling from the 2025 microfinance peak, a proven underwriting engine in two-wheelers and a wholesale legacy down to ~5% of the book. What it means
rows: Non-banking financial company: an RBI-regulated lender that cannot take current or savings deposits. The "upper layer" is the RBI's tier for the largest NBFCs, with bank-like rules.

New loans falling into Stage 3 in a period (before write-offs).
LTF's in-house AI underwriting engine and its portfolio-monitoring engine.
Commission LTF earns for selling insurance; credit life pays off a loan if the borrower dies. IRDAI is the insurance regulator.
Government credit-guarantee schemes for microfinance and small-business loans.
Capital ÷ risk-weighted assets (minimum 15% for NBFCs); Tier 1 is the core equity part (minimum 10%).

Price ÷ book value per share. Justified P/B = (ROE − g) ÷ (cost of equity − g). Residual income = book plus the present value of profit above the cost of equity.
